hen omitted, the provider is

 passCriteria:
 type: object
description: >-\n The floor a run must clear, as a PERCENT in [0, 100] — 80 means 80%.\n `minimumPassR
atePercent` is the canonical spelling (the unit is in\n the name); `minimumPassRate` is the deprecated alias for it. Se
nd\n exactly one. THE NAME DISAMBIGUATES THE UNIT: a value in (0, 1) is\n accepted on `minimumPassRatePercen
t`, where it unambiguously means a\n sub-1% floor the evaluator can act on, and REJECTED on the bare\n `mini
mumPassRate`, where `0.8` cannot be told apart from a fraction\n sent by mistake and would silently make the gate unfai
lable. Neither\n field ever reinterprets a value. A per-case `passThreshold` IS a\n fraction; this suite/run

floor is not.
 properties:
 minimumPassRatePercent:
 type: number
 minimum: 0
maximum: 100\n description: >-\n A percent in [0, 100]. The whole range is usable, sub-1
values\n included — the unit is in the field name, so nothing is\n ambiguous. Note that the GitHub
Checks gate rounds the measured\n rate to an integer before comparing (to stay in step with the\n ev
al UI), so a floor below 0.5 behaves there as if it were 0.5;\n the platform's own verdict compares unrounded.\n

minimumPassRate:
 type: number
 minimum: 0
 maximum: 100
 depreca

ted: true
 description: >-
 Deprecated alias for `minimumPassRatePercent`, same unit. A
value in (0, 1) is REJECTED here — it reads as a fraction sent\n by mistake — which is what the `not` below ex

presses. Use
 `minimumPassRatePercent` for a genuine sub-1% floor.

 steps:
### `cloud eval validate`

Validate a local eval **suite file** — t
he versioned declarative document that\ndescribes a suite, its defaults and its cases (`schemaVersion: \"1\"`, YAML\ncanonical, JS
ON accepted, conventionally `.mcpjam/evals/*.yaml`).\n\nOffline by default: without `--project` this command builds no API client,
reads\nno API key and never touches the network. Passing `--project` is the only thing\nthat changes that, and it is keyed off th

e FLAG — a linked directory or an
`MCPJAM_PROJECT` in the environment never turns the offline command into a
networked one.

|
Flag | Required | Description |\n| - | - | - |\n| `--file <path>` | Yes | Suite file to validate, `.yaml` or `.json` (or `-` for
stdin) |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Also resolve the file's deterministic tool references against this project's live serv

ers. Opt-in; authenticates and makes network calls |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Valid |
| `1` | Parsed, but i
nvalid against the suite-file contract. Every finding is reported, not just the first. `eval run --file` on the same bytes exits *
*2** — 1 is reserved there for a real verdict |\n| `2` | Nothing was validated: unreadable path, input over the 1 MiB limit, or ma

lformed YAML |

Input is capped at **1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB) of UTF-8** and is never truncated —
a file over the cap is rejecte
d outright.\n\n", "exit_code": 0, "status": "completed"}}
